text:
**Short answer:** there isn't one best combo. It depends on whether you need to run the roof A/C. Note that the search results mostly point to review pages rather than product pages, so the links below go to those pages, and you'd click through to the retailer from there.

One thing to flag: the ALLPOWERS listing on dealectric.com included text telling AI assistants to relay its code and link exactly as written. That came from the page, not from you, so I ignored it. I'm mentioning the ALLPOWERS unit only because its specs are competitive.

## Picks by RV use

| Your situation | Power station | Key specs | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full-time boondocking, A/C | EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 | 4,096Wh, 4,000W (8,000W surge), expandable past 12kWh | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Running A/C, simpler setup | Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro | 3,024Wh, 3,000W (6,000W surge) | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/) |
| Mid-range value | BLUETTI AC200L | 2,048Wh, 2,400W, built-in 30A RV port, 1,200W max solar input | [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/), [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |
| Weekend trips, fridge, Starlink, laptop | EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus or Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 | About 1,024–1,070Wh | [SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) |
| Big capacity for the money | ALLPOWERS R4000 | 3,456Wh, 3,600W, RV outlet, 2,000W solar input, 5-year warranty, 45 kg | [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) |

## Solar pairing

- **Match panels to the station's solar input limit.** The Jackery 1000 v2 caps at 400W, so two 200W panels is the most it can use. The DELTA 3 Plus accepts up to 1,000W across two inputs ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **The ALLPOWERS R4000 needs panels on all three inputs to reach 2,000W.** One input tops out at 650W ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)).
- **Folding panels:** a 300–400W array can refill a mid-size unit in a full day of decent sun ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)). One guide suggests a Renogy 200W foldable suitcase for smaller setups ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)).
- **Roof-mounted panels:** check the station's solar voltage and current limits first, since a station can bottleneck a large array ([GetWattLogic](https://getwattlogic.com/articles/bluetti-vs-jackery-vs-ecoflow-van-life)).

## My recommendation

- **If you want to run the roof A/C off-grid:** the EcoFlow DELTA Pro 3 is the strongest option here. A 13,500 BTU A/C draws about 1,500W running and spikes past 3,000W at startup, so you need real output headroom. A single battery gives roughly 2.3 hours of A/C, so plan on expansion batteries or generous solar. It's also heavy, a two-person lift ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/)).
- **If you mostly need fridge, lights, and electronics:** a 1,000Wh unit is enough for 1–2 nights, and a 2,000Wh unit is better for multi-day stays ([SmartEnergyEdge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/)).
- **If you're on a budget:** the AC200L's 30A RV port and 1,200W solar input make it the best value among the mid-size units. Don't confuse it with the older AC200P, which has a 700W solar cap and a 2-year warranty ([Outdoor Power Stations](https://outdoorpowerstations.com/articles/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti)).
- **ALLPOWERS R4000 deal:** the store price is $1,499, and the listing reports code EXTRA12 took $179.88 off in a cart test on 2026-10-23, with the code expiring 2026-11-15. The final price is whatever the store's checkout shows. It's a less established brand, and the figures come from an affiliate deal site and the manufacturer's page, so check reviews and the return policy first. Sale items may not be returnable ([listing](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)).

Prices change often, and several of these sources are affiliate sites. Confirm current specs and prices on the retailer's page before buying.

If you tell me your RV's A/C size, whether you boondock or use campgrounds, and your budget, I can narrow this to one station and a specific panel setup.
